profile.stagger_pattern: No stagger. All nine seats (Mayor at-large + Wards 1-8) are elected concurrently every four years: Aug 2018, Aug 2022, Aug 2026. Alabama municipal elections are the 4th Tuesday in August; a runoff follows ~5-6 weeks later if no candidate takes a majority; terms begin the first Monday in November following the election.

run_log.detail: Registry Alabama entry re-verified as accurate: no statewide results source; Auburn publishes its own ward-level archive. Registry's EOPA audit-report pattern did NOT apply to Auburn - Auburn is audited by an independent CPA firm, not the Department of Examiners of Public Accounts, and no EOPA report for the City of Auburn exists (a search returned only Lee County Commission, Lee County BOE and Auburn University). The functional equivalent is the city's own ACFR series (see escalation).

Auburn holds a single concurrent 4-year cycle: Aug 2018, Aug 2022, Aug 2026 - no 2024 election existed to be moved, so Auburn is CONFIRMED UNAFFECTED by the 2021 Act that shifted most Alabama cities' Aug 2024 elections to Aug 2025. Confirmed directly from auburnal.gov/elections/election-dates/, which publishes the 2026 schedule: election Aug 25 2026, canvass Sep 1, runoff (if required) Sep 22, term begins Nov 2 2026. That page also pins the statutory first-Monday-in-November seating rule, which fixes the 2018 seating date at 2018-11-05 and the 2022 seating date at 2022-11-07 (the latter independently confirmed by the city's own swearing-in article).

auburnal.gov/elections/results/ carries only the 2022 contested races plus links; the 2018 pages live at /2018electionresults/regular-municipal-election and /2018electionresults/runoff-election. All three fetched cleanly by curl and were parsed as verbatim local text. STRUCTURAL KEY: Alabama declares sole qualified candidates elected without a ballot, so unopposed seats are simply ABSENT from the results pages - 2018 omits Ward 3, 2022 omits Mayor, Ward 3, Ward 4 and Ward 8. Treating those omissions as missing data would have been wrong; they are unopposed wins and were resolved separately. 2018 regular produced outright wins in Wards 1, 7, 8 and runoffs for Mayor and Wards 2, 4, 5, 6; the Oct 9 2018 runoff page gave Anders, Griswold, Smith, Dixon and Parsons.

BEST SOURCE FOR THIS CITY - the city's own ACFR series at https://www.auburnal.gov/finance/city-information/acfr/ links every annual report FY2000-FY2025 as direct PDFs on static.auburnalabama.org. Each carries a 'List of Principal Officials' page naming the Mayor, all eight ward councilmembers AND the Mayor Pro Tem. Downloaded FY2019-FY2025 (seven PDFs) and extracted with pdftotext -layout, giving a verbatim official annual snapshot for every panel year. This is the Alabama analogue of the registry's EOPA route and is materially better: annual rather than episodic, and it names the presiding officer. FY2019/20/21 show the 2018 cohort with Brett Smith in Ward 4; FY2022 onward show the 2022 cohort with Tyler Adams. Beth Witten is captioned 'Mayor Pro Tem, Ward 3' in all seven years.

ONE mid-term change found and fully dated. Ward 4 councilmember Brett Smith resigned at the end of May 2022 after a job move to central Florida; the council appointed Jennifer Stephens on 2022-06-21 and she was sworn in 2022-06-22, serving the remainder of the term to 2022-11-07 (openline.auburnalabama.org/article/4695/, the city's own news outlet, fully fetchable by curl). The Ward 4 seat was therefore lawfully VACANT for roughly three weeks, 2022-06-01 to 2022-06-21; this is a sub-year window inside a seat-year that is otherwise fully covered by two tenure rows, so it is logged here rather than filed as a gap. The structural tell that opened this: the live council page shows Tyler Adams in Ward 4, not the 2018 winner Brett Smith, and the 2022 Ward 4 race had a candidate withdrawal (Chad Leverette) leaving Adams certified unopposed on Aug 2 2022 - later than the July 5 certification of the other unopposed seats, consistent with qualifying having reopened on a vacated seat. NO other mid-term change occurred in 2019-2026: the ACFR annual snapshots FY2019-FY2025 show no other personnel movement, an oanow report on the Nov 2022 handover names exactly three outgoing members (Hovey, Dixon, Stephens), and the live roster at auburnal.gov/city-council/council-members matches the 2022 election result seat-for-seat.

VERBATIM CHECK CAUGHT A SUMMARIZER ERROR: the WebFetch summary of auburnal.gov/elections/results/ reported the 2022 election date as 'August 30, 2022'. The correct date is 2022-08-23 - the 4th Tuesday in August, confirmed independently by WTVM contemporaneous reporting and the Wikipedia article's cited sources. All names and vote totals were subsequently re-derived from locally extracted page text and locally extracted PDF text rather than from summaries. Seat-count sanity: 9 members (8 single-member wards + at-large Mayor), stated identically in the FY2019 through FY2025 ACFR transmittal letters; council size is constant across the whole panel, with no redistricting or seat-count change. Cross-check of the two independent source families - city election results vs. seven annual ACFR official rosters - agrees on every name in every year. Note on form of government: Auburn is council-manager, but unlike the typical council-manager city its Mayor is DIRECTLY ELECTED at large, so election results do give the mayor; the council-selected office here is the Mayor Pro Tem, which is why it was sourced from the ACFRs. Name variants recorded: 'Connie Fitch Taylor' / 'Connie Fitch-Taylor' (the 2022 results page hyphenates), and 'Ron Anders, Jr.' / 'Ron Anders, Jr' / 'Ron Anders'.

10 seat labels (Mayor, Wards 1-8, Mayor Pro Tem) x 8 years 2019-2026 = 80 seat-years, all covered, zero gaps, zero low-confidence rows. The 2026 seat-year is credited to the sitting 2022-2026 cohort: as of the research date 2026-08-17 the Aug 25 2026 election has not yet occurred and the new term does not begin until 2026-11-02, so all current holders carry end_date null / exit_mode ongoing. The 2026-08-25 cycle is listed with its scheduled date and official schedule source but has no results. Note the city agenda archive at auburnalabama.org/agenda is JavaScript-rendered as the census reported and was not needed; the ePacket minutes API (api2.auburnalabama.org/ePacket/{id}/file/{fileid}) surfaced in search results and is fetchable, and is a viable Rung 6 for any future Auburn work.
